### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7ed5be3045e7e5e390cdbea4143b6432ec119f2a` — the merge of head `a0892887cc8251852c1602e3dd332a7141e72d58` into base `4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7ed5be3045e7e5e390cdbea4143b6432ec119f2a && git checkout 7ed5be3045e7e5e390cdbea4143b6432ec119f2a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9 a0892887cc8251852c1602e3dd332a7141e72d58 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9 && git merge --no-ff a0892887cc8251852c1602e3dd332a7141e72d58

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T22:53Z

Head-sha: 3644012a50212e8768fe2c256d813bdfdce5f4e7
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34878 (claim 6961939261, os-dev report 6963313201).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Fixes #34878`, base `main`. Five paths, +296/-15:
- `driver.ts` and `ask-skills.ts`;
- their tests in `ask-skills.test.ts` and `orchestrate.test.ts`;
- one `@objectstack/scenarios` patch changeset.

This stays inside the claim's file surface: `orchestrate.ts`, `app.ts` and the README are untouched, which keeps clear of #34985. Not governed. The branch is 7 behind `main`, with no overlap.

**CI.** It was still running when I read it (16 pending, 14 success, nothing failed). This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

**Half 1: a thrown turn is recorded and replays as the same failure.**
- **The recording side.** `RecordingDriver.ask` and `author` catch the throw, record `{ replyText: '', toolCalls: [], meta: {}, thrown: { name, message } }` under the step's key, and rethrow the original error. So a live run behaves exactly as before.
- **The replay side.** `RecordedDriver.ask` and `author` check `turn.thrown` right after the missing-turn check and before writing files or re-sending writes, then throw `RecordedThrowError` with the recorded `name` and `message`.
- **Each counting site lands where the live throw landed.** `errText` reads only `message`. Every site in `orchestrate.ts` that tells errors apart singles out only `MissingRecordingError` or `ReplayNotFaithfulError`:
  - questions (:1537), where anything else goes to `res.error`;
  - dataset questions (:1558);
  - operations (:1607, which rethrows to :1698);
  - confirmations (:1679);
  - authoring (:1049).

  `RecordedThrowError` is neither class, so it takes the `errText` branch at each one, as the live error did. The 4/5-live, 4/4-replay drift on a dataset row is gone. That is the row test's `{ passed: 1, total: 2 }`.
- **Replay verdicts stay unrecorded.** `thrownTurn` returns `undefined` for `MissingRecordingError` and `ReplayNotFaithfulError`. So recording a replay of a recording with a gap keeps the gap, and does not turn the gap into a recorded throw. A `RecordedThrowError` met while re-recording is kept as a thrown turn, which is right: the original failure carries forward.
- **Old recordings.** `thrown` is optional, so a recording without it replays as it did, and the control pin proves it on both trees.

**Half 2: the skill file must be spelled exactly `SKILL.md`.** `skillFileOf` reads the directory listing, so the spelling is the one on disk on every filesystem. An exact `SKILL.md` wins, and any other casing is returned and refused by `misspelt` with the path named (`name/skill.md` for a nested skill). A subdirectory with no skill file is still skipped, as before. The two crash cases from the premise (a case-insensitive `existsSync` true for `skill.md`, then `f.get(SKILL_FILE)!` undefined) are each pinned under a simulated case-insensitive `existsSync`, and both are red on `main`.

**Red first and ablation.** On the `main` sources with the tests kept: 5 red, including the two `toString` crashes and the row's `{1,1}` vs `{1,2}`. Deleting the replay rethrow turns the replay pins red. Both legs were restored by a blob-hash match.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. Clause-② is `yes (widening)`, not `no`.** `./runner` re-exports `driver.ts` whole (`export * from './driver.js'`), so this PR adds `ThrownTurn`, `RecordedTurn` and `RecordedThrowError` to a published entry point. It also widens `Recording.turns`' element type, with the optional `thrown` on the recording file a published reader parses. Every earlier scenarios changeset that added `./runner` exports declares `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and lists them, among them #33740, #33741, #33742 and #33818. One answer also moves for a replay reader: a replayed thrown turn now counts as an error instead of a missing turn. Please amend:
  - the claim;
  - the PR body;
  - the changeset's line to `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, with the three exports and the optional `RecordedTurn.thrown` named, all reached through `./runner`.

  Keep `Metadata-protocol: none` and the level at `patch`, because the level reads that line alone (the ruling on #25105).

### Notes
- N1. `skillFileOf` and the file walk both filter on `Dirent.isFile()`, so a `SKILL.md` that is a symlink is not seen. Before, it passed `existsSync` and then crashed in the walk. Now it is skipped, or refused as "holds no skill" when it is the only one. That is pre-existing, and the result is better than a crash, but the sentence does not say why. Not owed.

Next: the S1 amendment, which is text only and gets a delta read. Then o3-G lands once the three aggregates are green. No seat L2 is owed, unless the seat wants to rule Clause-② itself.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a0892887cc8251852c1602e3dd332a7141e72d58`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` alone). The PR has no published schema under `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path. The five paths are `.changeset/34878-scenario-thrown-turn-skill-case.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/{driver,ask-skills}.ts`, and their two tests. Inputs read: card #34878 (body, triage 6951618642, claim 6961939261, os-dev-report 6963313201, claim amendment 6963351666); PR #35007 (body, file list, net diff from merge-base `db1a05cdae` to this head); the L1-c records on the PR (6963367712, delta 6963512956); the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

The published surface is the `exports` map of `@objectstack/scenarios`. `./runner` maps to `src/runner/index.ts`, which runs `export * from './driver.js'`, so everything `driver.ts` exports is published. `ask-skills.ts` is not re-exported, but its `readAskSkills` is reached through the exported `ClaudeCodeDriver` (`driver.ts:375`, `opts.askSkillsDir`) and through the `objectstack-scenarios` bin.

- **New export `ThrownTurn`** (`./runner`), an interface of `{ name, message }`. Right. It is additive and is the type the recorded field needs.
- **New export `RecordedTurn extends ParsedTurn { thrown?: ThrownTurn }`** (`./runner`). Right. `ParsedTurn` is untouched, so every reader typed `ParsedTurn` compiles. A `RecordedTurn` is assignable to `ParsedTurn`. A `ParsedTurn` is also assignable to `RecordedTurn`, because the field is optional, so writes into `Recording.turns` also compile.
- **`Recording.turns: Record<string, ParsedTurn>` → `Record<string, RecordedTurn>`** (`./runner`). Right. This widens the recording file a published reader parses: one optional key, and nothing is narrowed. A recording written before this change has no `thrown` and replays as before, which the control pin shows. The in-repo readers are `export/cli.ts:119`, `export/exporter.ts:85`, `export/refresh.ts:261` and `export/transcript.ts:67` (`mergeRecordings`, which returns `Map<string, ParsedTurn>`). Each takes the subtype unchanged. `buildTranscript` looks a turn up only for a graded question (`transcript.ts:108-110`), and a thrown turn is never graded. `mergeRecordings` of an old recording, which has a gap, and a new one, which has a thrown turn, does not clash, because the gap has no key.
- **New export `RecordedThrowError`** (`./runner`), a class with `readonly key` that takes the recorded `name` and `message`. Right. It is additive. A consumer that wants to tell it apart must use `instanceof`, since `.name` is the recorded name. This class is how the runner's `errText` (it reads only `message`) and the `MissingRecordingError`/`ReplayNotFaithfulError` branches in `orchestrate.ts` count a replayed throw as the live one. The PR body's site table and L1-c both cite those branches. I read the cited lines only as context for this declaration, not as code under review.
- **Behaviour of exported classes.**
  - `RecordingDriver.ask`/`author` now record a thrown turn and rethrow the original error object, so live behaviour is unchanged.
  - `RecordedDriver.ask`/`author` throw `RecordedThrowError` before any file write or re-send (`driver.ts:752`, `:768`).
  - `thrownTurn` leaves `MissingRecordingError` and `ReplayNotFaithfulError` unrecorded.

  This is additive to what a recording can express, and it is the change the card's Done-when asks for. It is right.
- **No name collision under `export *`.** `git grep` at this head finds `ThrownTurn`, `RecordedTurn` and `RecordedThrowError` only in `driver.ts` and the changeset. None of the other thirteen modules `runner/index.ts` star-exports declares them, so no TS2308 ambiguity can drop one.
- **Not exported, correctly.** `thrownTurn` (driver.ts) and `skillFileOf` (ask-skills.ts) are module-private.
- **`--ask-skills` / `ClaudeCodeDriverOptions.askSkillsDir` accept set.** The listing-based match newly refuses some inputs on a case-sensitive filesystem that `main` ran:
  - a directory of skills in which one subdirectory holds `Skill.md` (`main` skipped that skill silently);
  - a top-level `skill.md` beside valid skill subdirectories.

  That would be a narrowing if the accept set were published, but it is not. `--ask-skills` and `askSkillsDir` came in with #34808 (merged 2026-11-17T13:38Z), and that changeset is still pending at this head (`.changeset/34687-ask-skills-dataset-cards.md`). The released `@objectstack/scenarios@18.5.0` CHANGELOG does not mention `ask-skills`. Tightening a surface that has never been released narrows no published accept set, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed. The refusal also makes the option's documented contract real on every filesystem, because a skill is a directory holding exactly `SKILL.md`. Right.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset**: one file, `'@objectstack/scenarios': patch`. The diff moves no other package. The package has released before (18.5.0), so a changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong. Right.
- **Level**: AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3, says: "The level follows the kind alone … `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`." `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, because the diff changes nothing a metadata author writes (no spec key, value or metadata type). So `patch` is the required level, not `minor`, even though a published package's types widen. L1-c cites the ruling on #25105 for the same reading.
- **Clause-② line**: `Clause-②: yes (widening: published @objectstack/scenarios ./runner types ThrownTurn, RecordedTurn and RecordedThrowError, plus one optional field on Recording.turns)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body, and the two are identical.
  - `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads the value `yes`. `readArmToken` reads the arm `widening` as the first token inside the parenthesis, because the lookahead admits the following `:`.
  - The export list matches exactly what the diff adds to `./runner`: three new exported names and one optional field on the element type of `Recording.turns`. Strictly, the field is `RecordedTurn.thrown`, the element type of `Recording.turns`. The line's wording is accurate.
  - The line names nothing the diff does not publish and omits nothing it does.
  - The precedents agree: the scenarios CHANGELOG entries b76df9a and 1e77fef declare `./runner` export additions the same way.
- **Gates on this head**: `Check Changeset` (both runs) succeeded, and so did `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)` (both runs) and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. At 23:07Z these had also succeeded: `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · ESLint`, every other `Lint ·` family, `Build Core`, and `Test Core` 4/10, 5/10 and 6/10. No shard 7/10 to 10/10 run exists on this head, after `Plan Test Core shards` succeeded. No check-run has failed.
- **Consumer type-checks**: no existing consumer breaks. Every in-repo reader of `Recording` is listed under ①. No other workspace package depends on `@objectstack/scenarios`: outside its own `package.json`, the name appears only in `.changeset/config.json` and `turbo.json`. `Type Check · workspace` is green on this head. `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Test Core` 1/10, 2/10 and 3/10 were still `in_progress` when I read them. The verdict below holds on condition that those four finish green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0] (Clause-② no vs yes (widening))**: answered. The seat ruled B, and the claim amendment 6963351666, the PR body and the changeset now carry `yes (widening)` with the export list. I concur on the diff: `./runner` star-exports `driver.ts`, so the three types and the optional field are a published widening. This closes L1-c's S1 (6963367712), and the delta 6963512956 is on this head.
- **open_questions[1] (dev-written HTML comments in the PR body)**: answered as no contract effect. The leading attribution comment and the trailing signed comment are not part of any published surface or declaration line. The Clause-② and Metadata-protocol lines are plain, line-initial text outside any comment, and the PR-body guards passed. Which process rule governs is a seat-protocol matter, outside this record. No finding.
- **out_of_scope_findings**: both are acknowledged and owe nothing on this head.
  - `skill-evals/cases.ts:145` silently skips a wrongly cased bundle on a case-sensitive host. It is outside the claim's file surface and reads the published `skills/` catalogue, which has its own gates. The seat may file it as its own card.
  - A recording of a replay keeps a `ReplayNotFaithfulError` gap. That behaviour is unchanged and is pinned as the reason `thrownTurn` excludes that error.
- **Note, not owed (forward compatibility)**: an older `@objectstack/scenarios` that replays a recording written by this version reads a `thrown` turn as an answered empty turn. It is graded rather than errored, so the old runner's row differs. Recordings are produced and replayed by the same runner version, and the published surface makes no cross-version replay promise, so this is not a finding.
- **Note, not owed**: L1-c N1 (a symlinked `SKILL.md` is filtered out by `Dirent.isFile()` and reads as "holds no skill") stands as a note.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5)**: not applicable. The diff touches an in-memory recording map, a JSON recording file and a filesystem listing. It adds no id materialisation, no in-app join and no data query that SQL could push down. No finding.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none.

Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: PASS**
